content: Breast shells are hollow, plastic devices designed to be worn inside a bra to prevent the nipple from becoming flattened. The design of the shell is slightly concave to fit the natural contour of the breast, although they may still be noticeable under tight-fitting clothing. Breast shells are made to be disassembled for cleaning, and frequent washing is essential. This is because the shells can cause the breast to sweat, creating an environment conducive to bacterial growth, which may lead to irritation or infection. These devices are often used to protect nipples that are engorged or sore during breastfeeding. Additionally, breast shells can help an inverted nipple to protrude, making it easier for the baby to latch. If the purpose of the shell is to prepare the mother for breastfeeding, it is generally recommended to use them during pregnancy. However, it is important to note that wearing breast shells during this time may increase the leakage of breast milk or colostrum. Some studies indicate that using breast shells on inverted nipples might actually interfere with the mother’s ability to breastfeed effectively. Breast shells can also serve as a means to collect milk when the baby has not fully emptied the breast during feeding. It is important to distinguish breast shells from nipple shields. Nipple shields are specifically designed to be used during breastfeeding to assist with latching, whereas breast shells are intended for use either in preparation for breastfeeding or after feeding.
